In this world, there are people who are born happy.
Some admire them.
Some find them strange.
Others find them to be quite normal.
Fantine is one of those naturally happy people.
Fantine and Iola are sisters from Bloomville.
The elder sister, Fantine, followed in their father’s footsteps and became a perfumer, while the younger sister, Iola, took after their mother and became a shepherdess.
Fantine couldn’t understand why Iola worried so much over a certain boy named Lycus, and Iola couldn’t understand why Fantine was always so happy.
Iola didn’t just worry about Lycus—she began worrying about Fantine, too.
She wondered if her sister might be ill.
For the first time, Fantine felt a little worried. She took her little Nimbi and went to Driftwise Meadow, hoping to relax a little while searching for perfume ingredients.
Not long after arriving, her Nimbi grew upset.
Holding her upset Nimbi, Fantine felt a sorrow she had never known before, and let the Nimbi go.
She couldn’t understand. Was her joy what made her different? Was being sad really the right way to be?
It wasn’t until the bittersweet bloom blossomed that Fantine suddenly understood.
If Fentufts were happy, and she was happy too, then why shouldn’t a happy Fantine be together with the happy Fentufts?
She even began to wonder—was she actually just a tall, slender Fentuft?
